questions.q: What is a GitHub issue used for, according to this lesson?
options: Tracking a unit of work — a bug, request, or question — that may or may not become a pull request
Only for reporting security vulnerabilities
Replacing commits entirely
Storing large binary files
questions.explain: An issue is where work lives before it has a diff — it might later become a PR, or be resolved without ever needing one.

questions.q: What are labels used for on GitHub issues?
options: Filtering and categorizing issues without reading every title
Automatically closing issues after a set time
Assigning a dollar cost to each issue
Encrypting the issue's contents
questions.explain: Labels like bug, data-quality, or p0 let you filter a long issue list at a glance instead of reading every title.

questions.q: What does a GitHub project (board) do?
options: Arranges issues and pull requests into status columns like Backlog, In Progress, and Done
Automatically merges all open pull requests
Deletes stale issues after 30 days
Replaces the need for a repository
questions.explain: A project board is a column-based view where dragging a card between columns updates its status — a live view of actual progress.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend for a data team's label set?
options: Small and specific — like data-quality, new-metric, pipeline-failure — not a large taxonomy nobody remembers
As many labels as possible to cover every conceivable case
No labels at all — they add unnecessary overhead
Only GitHub's default bug and enhancement labels, never custom ones
questions.explain: A small, specific label set that people actually use consistently beats a large taxonomy nobody remembers.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what breaks down as a team grows past three or four people?
options: Ad hoc coordination like 'just Slack me when it's done'
Git itself stops working
GitHub repositories become read-only
Pull requests can no longer be created
questions.explain: Ad hoc coordination works fine at small scale but breaks down around three or four people, which is exactly what issues and boards are built to fix.
